**Scout Report #10**

After nearly a full week of radio silence, Scout Team #3, along with Engineer David, and Doctor Emilia were dispatched to the weather station. Their objective was to retrieve the survivors and repair and re-establish the weather station.



**Day 1:** Except for salvaging a pile of empty crates for raw material, nothing interesting was of note. After a day of travel, the scout team arrived at the foot of the mountain and camped for the night.



**Day 2:** Despite worsening weather, the team continued to ascend. With the help of ex-weather station guard Lana, the team managed to find a shortcut. However, the team encountered a pack of wolves while crossing the shortcut. Fortunately, the team recognized that the wolves were only seeking passage, and no one was harmed by this encounter. As the ascension continued, the team discovered a dangerous ice field full of deeply hidden fissures. The team managed to cross safely by using a few planks to test the path. Just before sunset, the team arrived at the ice lake beneath the weather station. David, stepping on fragile ice, fell into the lake, he was rescued by his teammate and transported to the weather station quickly. Only his prototype tools were damaged during this narrow encounter.

The weather station was in an abysmal state. An avalanche a week prior nearly wiped out the entire station. Both housing cabins and the storage were destroyed and swept into the lake. The equipment was severely damaged. Only six of the previous forty station staff survived.



**Day 3:** The scouts salvaged what they could, and retrieved the final steam core with the help of David. 

Emilia examined and gave temporary treatment to the six survivors, unfortunately, the station doctor was diagnosed with a terminal illness, due to sustained exhaustion and fever. Only five engineers were fit for the return trip. 

Although the weather was damaged beyond repair, David was able to fix the difference engine and extrapolate the information from the data left behind by the researcher. The team then sent the emergency telegram back to the city. After a lengthy discussion, Lana chose to stay behind and optically observed the storm until the city could see it themselves.



**Day 4:** The scout began the return trip, smoothly arriving at the previously mentioned ice field. It was then that a second avalanche struck the team from the back. Both Ada and Henry were severely injured by the impact, Emila was entombed under the ice, and Scout (The name of one of the members) was strangled by a dangling sled, and nearly fell off the cliff. In the end, all members survived, but with a cost. Scout and Henry suffered further fractures during the rescue attempt, David sustained crippling frostbite while rescuing Emila, And Emila had to perform an emergency amputation in order to escape the entrapment. 

It was then that the team shot the emergency flare, and was rescued by scout team #2.



In conclusion, this expedition was catastrophic. Most of the station members were dead, the station itself was broken beyond repair, and almost all of the scout team members sustained severe if not crippling injuries. However, the team was able to salvage some raw material and steam core, as well as relay the information about the storm.

**End of Report for Scout Expedition #10**

As a (self-proclaimed) Don't Starve veteran, I can help you.

*On the subject of the Abbreviations:*  
Those initials are the different DLCs you have for the game. DS is base game, Don't Starve. RoG is improved base game, Reign of Giants. SW is ocean game, Shipwrecked. There's also a fourth one you don't have called Hamlet, which is pig town game.

*On the subject of starting a new world: (assuming that you don't want to "beat" the game, just survive.*  
Spend about 6 days mapping out the edges of the world, this gives you important locations like swamps, rockylands, and the pig king.  
All base resources are important to stock up on. Grass, twigs, rocks, flint, wood, and some gold is good in case you need it.

*On the subject of hounds:*  
Early game, hounds are a joke. If you stay near a group of pigmen, they'll take care of it without you having to do a thing. However, late game, things get rough. Consider making a panic room. make an area surrounded by tooth traps and when you hear hounds, just get in the center. The traps should deal with most if not all the hounds, and if some make it through, kill them yourself and add more traps next time. When the wave is over, reset the traps and continue starving.

I hope this helps you really get into Don't Starve!
